title: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)
summary: Characterized by persistent depressed mood and/or loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia) for at least 2 weeks, accompanied by significant distress or impairment.
criteria: Criterion A: 5 or more symptoms present during same 2-week period with change from previous functioning; at least one must be (1) Depressed mood or (2) Loss of interest/pleasure.
1. Depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day (feeling sad, empty, hopeless).
2. Markedly diminished interest or pleasure in all or almost all activities most of the day.
3. Significant weight loss when not dieting or weight gain, or decrease/increase in appetite.
4. Insomnia or hypersomnia nearly every day.
5. Psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day (observable by others).
6. Fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day.
7. Feelings of worthlessness or excessive, inappropriate guilt.
8. Diminished ability to think, concentrate, or indecisiveness.
9. Recurrent thoughts of death, suicidal ideation without a specific plan, or a suicide attempt.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out manic/hypomanic episodes (bipolar), substance/medication-induced depressive disorder, depressive disorder due to another medical condition (e.g. hypothyroidism), and normal bereavement/grief.

title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD)
summary: Excessive, uncontrollable anxiety and worry about multiple everyday events or activities occurring more days than not for at least 6 months.
criteria: Criterion A: Excessive anxiety and worry occurring more days than not for at least 6 months about a number of events/activities.
Criterion B: The individual finds it difficult to control the worry.
Criterion C: Associated with 3 or more of the following 6 symptoms (with at least some symptoms present for more days than not for past 6 months):
1. Restlessness or feeling keyed up or on edge.
2. Being easily fatigued.
3. Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
4. Irritability.
5. Muscle tension.
6. Sleep disturbance (difficulty falling/staying asleep, restless unsatisfying sleep).
duration_requirement: More days than not for at least 6 months.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out Panic Disorder (anxiety not confined to paroxysmal attacks), Social Anxiety Disorder, OCD, PTSD, hyperthyroidism, and caffeine/substance use.

title: Panic Disorder
summary: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks accompanied by persistent concern or worry about additional attacks and maladaptive changes in behavior.
criteria: Criterion A: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks — an abrupt surge of intense fear or intense discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes.

Requires 4 or more somatic/cognitive symptoms: Palpitations/pounding heart, sweating, trembling/shaking, shortness of breath/smothering, feelings of choking, chest pain/discomfort, nausea/abdominal distress, dizziness/unsteadiness/lightheadedness, chills or heat sensations, paresthesias (numbness/tingling), derealization (unreality) or depersonalization (detached from oneself), fear of losing control or 'going crazy', fear of dying.
Criterion B: At least one attack has been followed by 1 month (or more) of persistent concern/worry about additional panic attacks or significant maladaptive change in behavior related to attacks.
duration_requirement: At least 1 month of persistent worry or behavioral changes following an attack.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out cardiac arrhythmias, pheochromocytoma, vestibular dysfunction, stimulant toxicity, and agoraphobia without panic.

title: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) & Complex PTSD
summary: Development of characteristic intrusion, avoidance, cognitive/mood alterations, and hyperarousal symptoms following exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence.
criteria: Criterion A (Stressor): Direct exposure, witnessing, learning of trauma to close relative/friend, or repeated extreme exposure to aversive details.

Criterion B (Intrusive symptoms - 1+ required): Recurrent distressing memories, distressing dreams, flashbacks/dissociative reactions, intense psychological distress at exposure to internal/external trauma cues.
Criterion C (Avoidance - 1+ required): Avoidance of trauma-related memories/thoughts/feelings, or avoidance of external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities).

Criterion D (Negative alterations in cognitions and mood - 2+ required): Inability to recall key features, persistent negative beliefs about oneself/world, distorted blame of self/others, pervasive negative emotional state, diminished interest, detachment/estrangement from others, persistent inability to experience positive emotions.

Criterion E (Alterations in arousal and reactivity - 2+ required): Irritability/angry outbursts, reckless/self-destructive behavior, hypervigilance, exaggerated startle response, concentration problems, sleep disturbance.
ICD-11 CPTSD Specifier: Includes all PTSD criteria plus severe disturbances in self-organization (affect dysregulation, negative self-concept, and relational difficulties).
duration_requirement: Duration of disturbance is more than 1 month.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out Acute Stress Disorder (symptoms < 1 month post-trauma), Adjustment Disorder, MDD, BPD, and traumatic brain injury (TBI).

title: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD)
summary: Presence of obsessions (recurrent, persistent intrusive thoughts/urges), compulsions (repetitive behaviors/mental acts performed to reduce anxiety), or both, causing marked distress and consuming >1 hour daily.
criteria: Obsessions: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images experienced as intrusive and unwanted, causing marked anxiety or distress. The individual attempts to ignore or suppress them with other thoughts or actions.

Compulsions: Repetitive behaviors (hand washing, ordering, checking) or mental acts (praying, counting, repeating words silently) driven in response to an obsession or rigid rules, aimed at preventing or reducing anxiety.
Time consumption: Obsessions or compulsions are time-consuming (e.g., take more than 1 hour per day) or cause clinically significant impairment in social/occupational functioning.
duration_requirement: Time-consuming (>1 hour/day) and persistent over weeks to months.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out GAD (worries about real-life concerns), MDD (rumination), Body Dysmorphic Disorder, Trichotillomania, Tic disorders, and Delusional disorder.

title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
summary: A persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development, with several symptoms present prior to age 12 in 2 or more settings.
criteria: Inattention (6+ symptoms for children, 5+ for adults 17+): Fails to give close attention to details/makes careless mistakes; difficulty sustaining attention; does not seem to listen when spoken to directly; fails to finish tasks/instructions; difficulty organizing tasks and activities; avoids tasks requiring sustained mental effort; loses things necessary for tasks; easily distracted by extraneous stimuli; forgetful in daily activities.

Hyperactivity and Impulsivity (6+ symptoms for children, 5+ for adults): Fidgets with hands/feet or squirms; leaves seat when remaining seated is expected; runs/climbs in inappropriate situations or feelings of restlessness; unable to engage in leisure activities quietly; 'on the go' or acts as if 'driven by a motor'; talks excessively; blurts out answers; difficulty waiting turn; interrupts or intrudes on others.
Cross-situational requirement: Symptoms must be present in two or more settings (e.g., at home, school/work, with friends).
duration_requirement: Persistent for at least 6 months, with onset before age 12.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out Learning Disorders, Anxiety Disorders, MDD, Bipolar Disorder, Sleep Apnea, and Substance Use.

title: Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD)
summary: A pervasive pattern of instability of interpersonal relationships, self-image, and affects, and marked impulsivity beginning by early adulthood.
criteria: 5 or more of the following 9 criteria:
1. Frantic efforts to avoid real or imagined abandonment.
2. Pattern of unstable and intense interpersonal relationships characterized by alternating between extremes of idealization and devaluation ('splitting').
3. Identity disturbance: markedly and persistently unstable self-image or sense of self.
4. Impulsivity in at least 2 areas that are potentially self-damaging (spending, sex, substance abuse, reckless driving, binge eating).
5. Recurrent suicidal behavior, gestures, threats, or self-mutilating behavior.
6. Affective instability due to a marked reactivity of mood (intense episodic dysphoria, irritability, or anxiety lasting hours to days).
7. Chronic feelings of emptiness.
8. Inappropriate, intense anger or difficulty controlling anger.
9. Transient, stress-related paranoid ideation or severe dissociative symptoms.
duration_requirement: Pervasive and inflexible across situations, persisting since early adulthood.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out Bipolar II disorder (mood shifts in BPD are rapid and triggered by relational cues), Complex PTSD, MDD, and substance use disorders.

title: Insomnia Disorder
summary: A predominant complaint of dissatisfaction with sleep quantity or quality, associated with difficulty initiating sleep, maintaining sleep, or early-morning awakening with inability to return to sleep.
criteria: Criterion A: Dissatisfaction with sleep quantity or quality with 1+ of: (1) Difficulty initiating sleep, (2) Difficulty maintaining sleep (frequent awakenings), (3) Early-morning awakening with inability to return to sleep.
Criterion B: Sleep disturbance causes clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, educational, academic, or behavioral functioning.
Criterion C: Sleep difficulty occurs at least 3 nights per week.
Criterion D: Sleep difficulty is present for at least 3 months.
Criterion E: Occurs despite adequate opportunity for sleep.
duration_requirement: At least 3 nights per week for at least 3 months.
differentials_and_exclusions: Rule out Sleep Apnea, Restless Legs Syndrome, Circadian Rhythm Sleep-Wake Disorders, and substance/caffeine use.
